about: Fan's vocabulary: one word per thing, and the one way each is spelled in every layer. The terms are the business, the verbs and plain words are the grammar that joins them. tools/dev/vocab.js reads this file: it checks every name in the page (files, top-level names, locals, fields, CSS classes, ids, tokens, storage keys, records, topics, elements and the labels on screen), writes SPEC.md section 2's table, and tools/dev/rename.js applies renames. test/vocab.test.js holds the line.

spelling.about: A term is written once, in words. Each layer spells it by rule, so no layer needs its own name for it.
spelling.element: fan-<words joined by ->: an on-screen term's element, <fan-game-card>
spelling.css: <words joined by ->: game-card, and its parts game-card-head
spelling.js: <camelCase>: gameCard, and with a verb, drawGameCard
spelling.const: <UPPER_SNAKE>: GAME_CARD, a fixed table or number
spelling.rust: <snake_case>: game_card, the connector's modules, functions and fields
spelling.records: <camelCase> fields; collections keep their stored names (a term's stored)
spelling.files: <words joined by ->: a term that has its own file is named for it

rules: A name is made of words from this file: terms (or a term's short), verbs and plain words. A word that isn't here is either a new term, added with its meaning, or the wrong word.
One meaning per word. A word with two meanings is listed under homonyms with the meaning each place has, until one of them is renamed.
A term's short is its spelling inside names only where the full term would make every name long: hc for Handicap, ml for Moneyline. A short is never a word of its own.
A retired name (a term's was) never comes back in new code; the check names the term to use instead.
A local (a function's own variable or parameter) of one or two letters is a placeholder, not a name: g for a game, t for a ticket. Any longer local is a name like any other.
A field of one or two letters is allowed only when fields lists it with what it holds. A field that starts with a capital is data, not a name: a team, a position, a station (KC, Chiefs, WR, KUSA).

A name that isn't Fan's to choose is left alone: the web platform's (tools/dev/platform-names.json) and an outside source's fields (outside). An outside source's text is never written into the page as markup.
A label on screen is English, so its words are free; a retired name in one isn't.
Stored names (record collections and fields, storage keys) change only with a migration, so a term keeps its stored name and the code maps it in one place.

A person is named by role, never by name: the User, an Alpha user. No one's name goes into a name, a comment, a label or anything that ships (the user, Nov 5 2026: "We never want to use anybody's name").

parts.means: Follow the games: slates, scores, previews, telecasts and the wall. Free, and on for everyone.
Keep the user's bets: the wager ticket, Saved tickets, the totals and the Ledger. Bet tracking's checkbox.
Show the markets' prices on the cards, live, from the user's own pull. Needs the connector.
Send orders to an exchange: Place, Execute and algos. Needs the connector and a key.

terms.means: The app; and the Fan button, which opens the settings window.
Fan's front end, the one web page in src/, wherever it's served from.
A person who runs Fan with their own data, on their own machine. Fan's people are named by role, never by name.
A user Fan does specific, rapid cycles with: builds for their setup, fixes from their reports. Their value is that they're a user; never named.
The public page on GitHub Pages, where every copy of Fan follows.
The program on the user's computer that serves the page and holds what a browser can't: records, keys, orders, refreshes, algos.
The connector's executable. A new program is a new minor version and a download.
The connector's JavaScript runtime, which runs the page's calculations and line refreshes with no page open.
What the page runs in, and what fills its sockets: the connector, or the browser alone.
A slot the host fills: Fan.store, Fan.lines, Fan.trader, Fan.screens.
The records' socket: get, list, set, add, update, del, watch.
The stored facts: tickets, fills, slates, balances, checks. Nothing calculated is stored as a fact.
A daily copy of the records, newest 30 kept; and a browser's own file copy.
Fan's one number, major.minor.patch: the user's, a new program, a page release.
Publishing a version: ship.js, to both repos and the site.
The user's connector serving the working copy instead of the site's page: page-dev.txt in its data folder.
A Kalshi demo key: orders to Kalshi's demo exchange, shown as DEMO everywhere orders are.
Under way (a game: kickoff to 3.5 hours after), or on the live exchange (a key, a fill).
A Kalshi API key, held by the connector, never by the page. Also a record's id in a map (a plain word).
A strip button: a week or day on top; Graphs and the sections on the bottom strip. Exactly one is active.
The full-width band at the top or bottom of the window, two rows high.
The strip at the top: the week or day tabs, the league picker and the Fan button.
The strip at the bottom, whose buttons belong to the active tab.
The line just above the bottom strip: byes, the slate's notes, the version, DEMO and DEV.
Between the top strip and the info line: where the cards, the stack, a section and the game detail go.
The main view's two columns: game cards on the left, the stack on the right. The column divide is the stack's left edge.
The right-hand column: totals, Saved tickets and the wager ticket, or the risk detail.
The league's photo under a dark wash, from the top strip to the bottom strip.
The window the Fan button opens, over the usable space, with its tabs down the left.
The settings window's first tab: what runs where, with a card per part, the connector box and the outside services.
The connector box's gear, which turns green while every status is green or off.
A pill naming a part of the system and its state: green working, amber a warning, red a problem, grey off. A tick means verified.
The league on screen, on the top strip; pressed, a tile per league.
Season stats, Handicap, Code or Ledger: a tab with a page of its own instead of a slate. Its buttons are its views.
What fills the usable space: the week, Graphs or a section; and a section's own views.
A placeholder page that says what isn't built. Never made-up numbers.
A short message that shows for a moment and goes.
NFL, NBA, NHL, MLB, NCAA football or basketball: its slates, teams, Kalshi series and looks.
A league's year of games; the current one is in shared.js.
An NFL slate, Wednesday to Tuesday.
A daily league's slate: an Eastern-time day of NBA or NHL games.
The games of one tab: an NFL week or an NBA day; stored in the slate collection.
One game: visitor @ home, kickoff, networks, lines, score. Named Visitor -spd @ Home, week first in conversation (7:Chiefs@Seahawks).
A league's team: code, name, nickname, colors, helmet or logo.
The away team, written first.
The home team, written after the @.
When a game starts; a slate's games are grouped into kickoff windows.
A finished game, and its score. A saved final is never overwritten.
The game's points so far, from the browser's own ESPN pull.
A team with no game in an NFL week, shown on the info line.
One game's box on a slate: badges, lines, score, the gutter, and with Track the bets row.
The game card's column of icon buttons: Game preview, Live telecast, Tape, Box score, Risk detail.
A team's chip on a game card, in a named style (Plain, License).
An NFL team's helmet image; a logo in other leagues.
The per-game page opened from a card's Game preview: the teams' rows, schedules, injuries, weather, script.
A final game's replay: the NFL's condensed replay, a daily league's ESPN recap.
A game's ESPN box score.
A player's injury report, by severity.
A game's forecast, on the game detail.
A game on TV: what a card's Live telecast opens, through its network's source.
What a game is on: CBS, Fox, ABC, ESPN; ESPN's list plus a few rules (the Monday night ABC rule).
Where a network comes from: a link from a streaming service, a tuner's channel, or none.
An antenna tuner on the home network; its channels are sources.
Games put on the user's computers' monitors, from the top of the Telecasts tab.
One of the user's other computers, joined to the wall, with its monitors and windows.
A tablet or phone paired on the home network: Watch and the wall only.
The connector's home-network port, where the wall's screens and remotes come in.
A game's prices: moneyline, spread and total. The closing line is the permanent record; live lines are separate.
A bet on who wins.
A bet on the margin; the visitor's points, positive when the visitor is the underdog.
A bet on the combined points, over or under.
The team the market expects to win.
The other team.
A price as American odds (+150, -120) or decimal.
What a contract costs, in cents; and the Price part.
The price with the vig taken out, by the methods' de-vigging.
The house's margin in a price.
A price that pays at least the fair price (positive); expensive (negative) is the other side. Never the odds' sign.
An exchange's contract for one outcome, by ticker.
An exchange's id for a market.
An exchange Fan pulls prices from or sends orders to: Kalshi, Polymarket US.
The exchange Fan trades on.
A second venue, for prices.
A venue's best bid and ask for one market, at one moment.
Where every browser pulls its own schedules, scores, stats and injuries.
The cheapest asks across venues for each strike, for hedge suggestions.
The connector's in-game order books for the games on screen.
The connector pulling lines and finals on its timer (lines.js).
Home score minus visitor score. The P/L graph's axis is the favorite's margin.
The margins NFL games land on most: 3, 6, 7, 10, 14. The step function.
The underdog wins; small by 1 to 3, big by 4 or more.
The favorite's moneyline and the underdog's points both win.
Two of a game's prices that together pay in more outcomes than they cost (8.3).
The entry form: sportsbook, amount, game, bet type, side, line and price, then Book or Place.
One recorded bet, one row of Saved tickets.
The list of tickets, with its Wagers and Summary tabs and search.
The card over the stack: risk, win and P/L for the games in view.
Where a bet was made: a sportsbook, or an exchange.
What a ticket cost, fee included once.
A bet made with a sportsbook's bonus money.
A one-leg bet.
A bet on several legs, all of which must win.
One of a parlay's bets.
Which way a bet goes: a team, over or under, yes or no.
A ticket's side and line in words; and choosing from a list (a verb).
Profit and loss.
What a ticket pays if it wins, stake included.
What can be lost: a game's worst case; Max risk and Max win over every score.
The graph card that takes the wager ticket's place when a game is selected.
Deciding a ticket's result from the final: won, lost, push, dead.
A sportsbook's cash as typed in, or Kalshi's as it reports.
The section with the accounts: Balances, By week, Open bets and the Kalshi check.
Comparing Kalshi's fills with the tickets, each order one ticket (calc.js reconcile).
A trade that happened at an exchange, as the exchange reported it.
A fill on a live key. Inviolable: no edit, no delete.
A fill Fan receives and owns but didn't place: the user's phone, say.
The connector's stream of fills to the page.
One unit of an exchange's market, paying a dollar if it wins.
The exchange's charge on a fill, counted once in a ticket's amount.
What Place, Execute or an algo sends to an exchange: ticker, side, count, price, immediate or cancel.
The wager ticket's button that sends an order to Kalshi.
The wager ticket's button that records a bet made elsewhere. Sends nothing.
The suggested bet's button that sends an order to Kalshi.
How many cents above the ticket's price Place may pay.
The one trade the page proposes for a game: a lock or a hedge.
A trade after which every outcome is a profit.
A trade that raises the worst case but leaves risk.
The money the suggested bet may put in, from RULES.
How much a hedge must raise the worst case to be suggested.
One of Kalshi's matching engines; an order is funded only from its market's shard.
The user's trading script, run by the connector's runtime: not approved, off, running or armed.
The section that runs algos: the grid, the editor, the console and the Methods row.
The Code section's log of what every algo prints, with a prompt.
A judgment calculation the user may replace: de-vigging, the margin model, EV, the Handicap's fit (Calc.METHOD_NAMES).
A fixed calculation: odds conversions, fees, P/L, settlement, the records check.
Expected value of a price at the fair chance.
The slate's chart of every game's prices against each other, with flagged pairs.
The section with Margins, Key numbers and Teams, and Trends under its graphs.
Past games filtered by situation, under Season stats.
A Trends filter over past games.
The section where the user sets a line for each game from DVOA, HFA and byes, against the market.
A team's efficiency rating, pulled by each user; the Handicap's coefficient multiplies the difference.
Home-field advantage, in points.
A coefficient set by least squares: vs all games, or one game's own (the outlier finder).
How far, as a percentage of absolute values, the market must differ from the user's line to light.

verbs.about: What a name does to a term. One verb per job: draw never render, delete never remove for records.
verbs.draw: make a term's elements from the data, replacing what was there
verbs.build: make a term's elements once, which draw then fills in place
verbs.fit: size a term to the space it has
verbs.show: make visible, or open a view
verbs.open: open a window, list or detail
verbs.toggle: flip between shown and hidden, on and off
verbs.pick: choose from a list (the user's choice)
verbs.select: make a game the selected one
verbs.set: replace a value, through its owner's setter
verbs.get: read a value that may need asking for
verbs.read: read from the records, a pull or a file
verbs.save: write to the records or storage
verbs.keep: write to this browser's own storage
verbs.delete: remove a record (short del, as the store's)
verbs.pull: ask an outside service: ESPN, Kalshi, Polymarket
verbs.send: send to the connector or an exchange
verbs.ask: send a question that waits for an answer
verbs.tell: send something that needs no answer
verbs.watch: follow a record or a size and act on each change (homonym: Watch the part)
verbs.apply: put a pulled or saved value into the page's state
verbs.use: put the user's own (methods, links) in Fan's place
verbs.make: build a value from others: a ticket from a fill
verbs.enter: put a price or bet onto the wager ticket
verbs.find: look for: the connector, a game by name
verbs.check: test a rule and say how it stands
verbs.run: run code: an algo, a check, an order
verbs.step: move to the next or previous
verbs.switch: change which one is current: week, league, mode
verbs.format: write a value as text (short fmt)
verbs.migrate: move stored data to a new shape
verbs.handle: act on an event or fill
verbs.define: declare a table the framework uses
verbs.can: a yes-or-no question about being allowed
verbs.on: whether a part, league or switch is on (trackingOn)
verbs.say: put words on the page: a note, a status
verbs.label: put labels on what's drawn
verbs.load: bring in code or data at the start
verbs.reconcile: compare two records of the same thing
verbs.persist: ask the browser to keep its storage
verbs.escape: make text safe for HTML (short esc)
verbs.join: join a screen to the wall, or a list into text
verbs.capture: save a picture of a window
verbs.leave: move away from, as off a league that's off
verbs.fold: fold a card or line into less room
verbs.spin: nudge a value by its arrows
verbs.arm: let an algo send its orders

words.about: Plain words: they mean what English says. Grouped only to be read.

abbreviations.about: Short forms of plain words, the only ones allowed. A term's short is with the term.
abbreviations.sxy: sum of x times y deviations
abbreviations.r2: R², the share of the variance a fit explains
abbreviations.ecl: a QR code's error correction level

stats.about: A team's stats, by the short names the page keeps them under in its own pull of ESPN (espn.js). Shown in a game's preview.
stats.stand: the team's standing, as 1st in AFC West
stats.ppg: points a game (NBA); power-play goals (NHL): see homonyms

fields.about: Short fields, kept short because records, the socket or a pull store them that way, or because one or two letters is the shape's own convention. Each says what it holds; changing one is a migration.
fields.t: a time: a game's kickoff, ISO
fields.k: a key (a view's), or a venue's ask on the socket, with tk its ticker
fields.v: a value; in the Handicap, a term's variable
fields.aa: a game's away team code, from ESPN
fields.ha: a game's home team code, from ESPN
fields.c1: the ladder's cheapest ask at its first rung
fields.c2: the ladder's cheapest ask at its second rung
fields.c3: the ladder's cheapest ask at its third rung
fields.kc: a Kalshi entry's contracts, cost and odds (the wager ticket)
fields.kd: a ladder row's Kalshi ask for the underdog
fields.kf: a ladder row's Kalshi ask for the favorite
fields.byeAdj: the saved Handicap's mark that its bye terms are in the adjusted form
fields.sx: a risk region's sum of x, for its center (with sT and n)

outside.about: Names that aren't Fan's to choose: the fields each outside source sends, as the page reads them. The web platform's own names are in tools/dev/platform-names.json. An outside source's text is never written into the page as HTML (test/vocab.test.js).

meanings: points a game, an NBA team's stat
power-play goals, an NHL team's stat
homonyms.decision: Kept for now: each browser's pull stores it under DAILY_STATS by league, so the league says which. A rename is the pull's next shape.

meanings: a wager, in plain English (gameBets, Suggested bet)
homonyms.decision: Kept: the part is always Bet with a capital in words and betOn in code; a wager in code is a ticket.
Book is the button; a sportsbook is sportsbook in code; the order book is the live book.
A fill is the exchange's; putting a bet on the wager ticket is enter, and drawing the settings window is draw.
Ticket is the record; the form is the wager ticket, wager-ticket in CSS and wagerTicket in code.
Stub is the placeholder; the ticket's foot is wager-ticket-foot.

meanings: the store's watch: follow a record
homonyms.decision: Kept for now: the store's watch is its contract's word. A rename is the store contract's next version.

meanings: the live exchange, as against demo
homonyms.decision: Kept: the context always says which; the key's is live key, a game's is live game.
A line is the prices; the info line is always info line in code; text lines are rows.

meanings: the game cards' strip of kickoff windows
homonyms.decision: Strip is the top or bottom strip; the cards' row is the slate's kickoff windows.

meanings: a drawn part in start.js's table
homonyms.decision: #panel is the slate; start.js's entries are draws.

meanings: the settings window, in old CSS (fan-window, fan-part)
homonyms.decision: fan- is the element namespace; the settings window's classes are settings-.
Kept: always with its noun in names (settingsWindow, telecastWindow, kickoffWindow).
Kept: the part is pricesOn in code, as it always was.

meanings: the visitor, as the records and the code name the teams (away, home)
an away trade: a fill placed outside Fan
homonyms.decision: Kept: away and home are the records' own; an away trade is always awayTrade in code.

meanings: a ticket's side and line in words
homonyms.decision: Kept: the ticket's is pickText; the verb takes an object (pickLeague).
